comments.text:
As of 2026, used to TF2 all the time since 2012, be it 14 years now, but today rarely do open the game because it is still much lore brutal, gory and high tech skill on certain gameplay options. I play Overwatch but it gets old real fast with the same few maps and routine feels limited and expected as gameplay entirely revolves around the objective and with shoet lived timer, looks nice and polished though, same goes to Marvel Rivals but both Overwatch and Rivals lack that "Unf" feeling of sheer violence like actually decapitating someone's head off, explode someone's entire body to pieces, blood spill everywhere, Team Fortress 2 provides me with that violence and dopamine that even if I choose the weakest class-character in the game I can still 1-shot a tank or brawl it out, but I stand a chance, you cannot do that in Overwatch, if you're Mercy and you try to 1v1 any single tank you WILL die unless you habe a team mate around to be able to fly towards, otherwise you're stuck with walking speed, and your best chance to 1v1 a Tank upclose is if you Ult (which allows Mercy to fly freely) then star shooting from above and even then that might just do nothing as Overwatch Tanks have self healing and way too much HP and/or deploy shields that have HP of their own to protect themselves or their team. In Rivals, some Support characters have the tools to survive and flee or flat out 1v1 a Tank but with much effort, in Rivals playing the weakest character still has a chance to survive or win against the strongest Tank in the game.
I stopped playing TF2 regularly not because I  experienced everything it had to offer, and the future copycats like Overwatch, Paladins, Rivals, etc are all more polished graphically and a lot more technical in different ways, the characters are so stuck to the obly moveset they have by default, while TD2 has each of the only 9 playable characters have unlockable weapons that completely change the playstyle of the character per weapon change, making everyone so unpredictable or harder to deal with. Team Fortress 2 is unhinged once you learn the gane physics and become an absolute unit if you adapt to that.
Overwatch plays with moba like logic of having timed cooldowns, unlimited ammo, absolute team dependency and limited player count that makes that more of a staple. In Team Fortress 2, competitive is 6v6, default servers are 12v12, community lobbies used to average 16v16 servers with quick respawn and people that ignored objectives just for the sake of killing each other nonstop and Team Fortress 2 is designed so you can fend off on your own without team dependency, even the Medic can fend off on his own as he has seriously high critical high rate on melee and usually 1 or two shots people that get to close, even tanky people. Of course you have to brawl it out, and Medic is the ONLY character in the gane with passive healing (OW Mercy used to be like this but now everyone in OW has this too).
There's no gore in Overwatch or Rivals, just blood splashes effects on most hits on organic beings, and clash marks on robot character, but walls or floor don't get covered in blood, there's no gunshot wounds on the character, you cannot decapitate people, you cannot truly explode someone to pieces. There's no real critical hit system, just "buffing" someone or self under certain conditions.
In Team Fortress 2 there is Critical Hits and Mini Crits, but most of all there is "RANDOM CRIT" system built into every character, so you can accidentally melt down someone with even the weapins tool in the game, or obliterate a whoke crowd of 16 people with a single critical hit rocket, be it random or buffed by a medic, bloody body parts everywhere. You cannot do that with regular attacks on these newer games, you need to "Ult" and even then the opposition could just survive it, way too team dependent.
I like Sombra in OW, Echo completely copies people and their abilities. But i like Spy a lot more.
Used to play Smash Bros WiiU/3DS, a bit of Melee then Ultimate, over 10 years, stopped on 2025, even when I got really good at it, I got... genuinely bored, sane routine too, dealing with cowardly tactics and zoning, spam based play styles, peoplr using items, etc, and eben when you outplay and beat them to oblivion, from joy it starts feeling like a chore, cannot enjoy it that much anymore.
comments.author: @SolidMetal8718

I play Overwatch but it gets old real fast with the same few maps and routine feels limited and expected as gameplay entirely revolves around the objective and with shoet lived timer, looks nice and polished though, same goes to Marvel Rivals but both Overwatch and Rivals lack that "Unf" feeling of sheer violence like actually decapitating someone's head off, explode someone's entire body to pieces, blood spill everywhere, Team Fortress 2 provides me with that violence and dopamine that even if I choose the weakest class-character in the game I can still 1-shot a tank or brawl it out, but I stand a chance, you cannot do that in Overwatch, if you're Mercy and you try to 1v1 any single tank you WILL die unless you habe a team mate around to be able to fly towards, otherwise you're stuck with walking speed, and your best chance to 1v1 a Tank upclose is if you Ult (which allows Mercy to fly freely) then star shooting from above and even then that might just do nothing as Overwatch Tanks have self healing and way too much HP and/or deploy shields that have HP of their own to protect themselves or their team. In Rivals, some Support characters have the tools to survive and flee or flat out 1v1 a Tank but with much effort, in Rivals playing the weakest character still has a chance to survive or win against the strongest Tank in the game.
I stopped playing TF2 regularly not because I  experienced everything it had to offer, and the future copycats like Overwatch, Paladins, Rivals, etc are all more polished graphically and a lot more technical in different ways, the characters are so stuck to the obly moveset they have by default, while TD2 has each of the only 9 playable characters have unlockable weapons that completely change the playstyle of the character per weapon change, making everyone so unpredictable or harder to deal with. Team Fortress 2 is unhinged once you learn the gane physics and become an absolute unit if you adapt to that.
Overwatch plays with moba like logic of having timed cooldowns, unlimited ammo, absolute team dependency and limited player count that makes that more of a staple. In Team Fortress 2, competitive is 6v6, default servers are 12v12, community lobbies used to average 16v16 servers with quick respawn and people that ignored objectives just for the sake of killing each other nonstop and Team Fortress 2 is designed so you can fend off on your own without team dependency, even the Medic can fend off on his own as he has seriously high critical high rate on melee and usually 1 or two shots people that get to close, even tanky people. Of course you have to brawl it out, and Medic is the ONLY character in the gane with passive healing (OW Mercy used to be like this but now everyone in OW has this too).
There's no gore in Overwatch or Rivals, just blood splashes effects on most hits on organic beings, and clash marks on robot character, but walls or floor don't get covered in blood, there's no gunshot wounds on the character, you cannot decapitate people, you cannot truly explode someone to pieces. There's no real critical hit system, just "buffing" someone or self under certain conditions.
In Team Fortress 2 there is Critical Hits and Mini Crits, but most of all there is "RANDOM CRIT" system built into every character, so you can accidentally melt down someone with even the weapins tool in the game, or obliterate a whoke crowd of 16 people with a single critical hit rocket, be it random or buffed by a medic, bloody body parts everywhere. You cannot do that with regular attacks on these newer games, you need to "Ult" and even then the opposition could just survive it, way too team dependent.
I like Sombra in OW, Echo completely copies people and their abilities. But i like Spy a lot more.
Used to play Smash Bros WiiU/3DS, a bit of Melee then Ultimate, over 10 years, stopped on 2025, even when I got really good at it, I got... genuinely bored, sane routine too, dealing with cowardly tactics and zoning, spam based play styles, peoplr using items, etc, and eben when you outplay and beat them to oblivion, from joy it starts feeling like a chore, cannot enjoy it that much anymore.
comments.author: @SolidMetal8718
